holidays.name: National Hot Sauce Day
holidays.description: A fiery celebration for anyone who believes food is simply a delivery system for capsaicin. Fans are encouraged to splash, drizzle, and dare their way through bottles of everything from mild jalapeño to tear-inducing ghost pepper.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday popularized by condiment fans and food-calendar sites. It grew out of the hot sauce boom in the US, with no single founder credited.
holidays.funFact: The Scoville scale, which measures the heat of chili peppers, was created in 1912 by pharmacist Wilbur Scoville, who originally used human taste testers diluting pepper extract until the burn disappeared.

holidays.name: National Blonde Brownie Day
holidays.description: A day for the underappreciated cousin of the chocolate brownie. Blondies are made with brown sugar, vanilla, and butter, and are often loaded with butterscotch chips, nuts, or white chocolate.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance created by dessert lovers and recipe sites to give the blondie its own moment in the spotlight.
holidays.funFact: Blondies are thought to predate chocolate brownies in some form, with early recipes resembling molasses-and-brown-sugar bar cookies from the 1800s.

holidays.name: National Answer Your Cat's Question Day
holidays.description: A day to finally respond to your cat's constant meowing, chirping, and judgmental staring. Owners are encouraged to treat each meow as a legitimate question and answer it with sincerity, snacks, or at least a polite conversation.
holidays.origin: A pet-themed unofficial holiday created by cat lovers and promoted on social media and fun-holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Research suggests adult cats rarely meow at other cats; they developed meowing largely to communicate with humans.

holidays.name: Celebration of Life Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to appreciating the gift of being alive. It encourages people to pause, reflect on their blessings, and perhaps do something spontaneous and joyful.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance from the fun-holiday calendar, often linked with remembering loved ones and cherishing the present, with no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: Celebration of life gatherings have become a popular alternative to traditional funerals, often featuring favorite music, stories, and even party food.

holidays.name: Sanctity of Human Life Day
holidays.description: A US observance recognized each year around this date, focused on reflection about the value of human life. Its themes are tied to the anniversary of the 1973 Roe v. Wade decision, and it is observed by many in the pro-life community.
holidays.origin: Presidential proclamations designated the day beginning in 1984 under President Ronald Reagan, and later administrations have issued or declined to issue them depending on their politics.
holidays.funFact: Unlike many fun holidays, this one has been formally proclaimed by multiple US presidents, making it one of the more official observances on the date.
